author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty on either published form
summary: Both published forms of the veterinarian directory accept an optional specialty named in the request and list only veterinarians holding it. The machine-readable form becomes a supported surface under this fresh id.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting either form without a specialty lists exactly as before: the page lists five per page, the machine-readable form holds every veterinarian with their specialties
Requesting either form with the optional `specialty` query parameter lists only veterinarians holding that specialty
A specialty name matches in full and disregards letter case; a name matching only part of a specialty name matches no veterinarian
A specialty no veterinarian holds yields the ordinary page or machine-readable form with no veterinarian listed, and the request succeeds with the normal success status
A `specialty` value that is empty or spaces alone behaves as though the parameter were absent, as an empty owner search does
Paging within a narrowed listing keeps the specialty in force: the page links carry it, and page counts and totals reflect the narrowed listing, not the whole directory
Narrowing changes which veterinarians appear, never the specialties shown against each
New behavior is covered by tests, one per numbered edge case in the PRD's Veterinarian directory section
non_goals: Any page control for choosing a specialty: no form, dropdown, or link set on either form. The choice travels in the request only
Free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits: NG-9 still declines it
Naming more than one specialty in a single request
Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: Fresh id minted per the owner: REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. The owner's URL contract is fixed: both `/vets.html` and `/vets` take an optional `specialty` query parameter. The PRD states this behaviorally and defers the routes and the parameter to system-design.md#contracts, matching how the document treats every other surface. Two questions are recorded open in the PRD rather than consulted: a visible control (owner says it may be a later request) and naming several specialties at once (narrowest reading taken: one).

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing `vet` feature package and introduces no new type, module, or layer. Narrowing follows the owner-search shape already recorded in system-design.md#contracts: a Spring Data derived query on the repository, a controller that normalizes the request parameter and selects between the narrowed and unnarrowed lookup, and a template whose pagination links carry the parameter. One decision is genuinely new and is recorded in an ADR: the specialty-filtered repository reads carry no cache annotation, because their key would otherwise be caller-supplied against a JCache with no configured size limit. Durable memory updated: system-design.md Contracts maps the five vet rows to REQ-VET-003, the VetRepository row states the cache split with an ADR back-link, and the Known Defects row declaring the machine-readable route requirement-less is removed because REQ-VET-003 now gives it one.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two derived finders traversing Vet -> specialties -> name with case-insensitive whole-name matching: one paged for the HTML surface, one unpaged Collection for the serialized surface. Neither carries @Cacheable; the two existing findAll reads keep theirs unchanged
VetController.showVetList gains an optional specialty request parameter, strips it, treats null-or-blank as absent, and selects between the narrowed and the existing unnarrowed paged lookup
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same optional parameter and the same blank handling, filling the existing Vets wrapper from whichever lookup applies
VetController.addPaginationModel places the in-force specialty on the model so the template can carry it on every pagination link
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty when one is in force; totals and page count come from the narrowed Page, so no template arithmetic changes
No change to Vet, Specialty, Vets, CacheConfiguration, the schemas, or the seed data. No new dependency

patterns.description: the sanctioned blank-parameter normalization: null becomes the broad case and a supplied value is stripped. Vets differ in one respect only -- a blank value routes to the unfiltered lookup rather than to a match-everything query, because the vet match is whole-name, not prefix
derived query returning Page, the pattern the two new vet finders follow
the existing paged lookup helper the narrowed lookup sits beside; page size stays a local variable per system-design.md#constants
the @Cacheable read convention the new finders deliberately depart from -- see the ADR

risks.risk: The existing pagination links use Thymeleaf's `__${...}__` preprocessing form, which performs no URL encoding. Interpolating a caller-supplied specialty into that form emits an unencoded value, so a name carrying a space or an ampersand yields a broken or parameter-injected link
risks.mitigation: Build the links with Thymeleaf's parameterized link syntax, which URL-encodes each parameter. Cover it with a test using a specialty name containing a space

risks.risk: A request naming the parameter twice is unstated in the PRD and no product answer will come
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading, recorded here rather than consulted: Spring binds repeated values into one comma-joined String, which matches no specialty in full, so the surface yields an empty listing with the normal success status -- exactly the edge-case-3 behavior. No extra code; assert it if cheap

risks.risk: Thymeleaf's rendering of a link parameter whose value is null is easy to get wrong, and could emit a bare parameter on the unnarrowed page
risks.mitigation: An emitted empty value is contract-equivalent to absent, so behavior is safe either way. Verify the rendered markup in the unnarrowed pagination test so the unnarrowed page stays byte-identical to today

risks.risk: Joining Vet to its specialties for the restriction while the association is eagerly fetched can duplicate rows and corrupt page totals
risks.mitigation: A whole-name match against a Set yields at most one matching specialty per veterinarian, so no duplicate arises. Assert totalElements and totalPages against the narrowed listing in the paging test; if the match ever becomes partial, distinct becomes mandatory

risks.risk: The blank-value branch in the controller can read as a business rule, which the architecture brief's Web controller row forbids and which the existing controller deviation does not extend to
risks.mitigation: Keep the branch to request normalization and lookup selection only -- strip, test for empty, choose a repository method. Every matching rule stays in the query. The owner precedent above is the shape to mirror

risks.risk: Both new surfaces echo a request-derived value; the narrowed page reflects it into generated URLs
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf output escaping stays on and the value never composes a resource path or query text, so no security-principles row is newly introduced. The threat model's XSS row gains this surface at doc-sync

notes:
URL contract for the implementer, fixed by the product owner: /vets.html?specialty=<name> narrows the page and pagination links carry the parameter; /vets?specialty=<name> narrows the serialized list and is a supported surface from this slice on; whole-name match ignoring case, never a prefix; no match yields the ordinary document with an empty list and HTTP 200; empty or whitespace-only behaves as absent; absent leaves both surfaces exactly as today; no form, dropdown, or link set is added to either surface.
ADR index: added the row for the non-goal ADR the PRD author flagged, and a row for the new caching ADR. The non-goal row belongs -- the index is the log's contents page and the file existed without an entry.
Brief tension worth naming, not blocking: the PRD defers 'the routes and the parameter' to system-design.md#contracts, while that file's own author note forbids transcribing parameter names because source is authoritative. Resolved in favor of the file's rule -- the VetController row names the narrowing and the surfaces, and the exact parameter contract lives in this record and in the tests.
Pre-existing and out of scope, confirmed not blocking: `python3 scripts/doctor.py check` reports `project-data: spec_version 0.1.0 does not match manifest 0.2.0` in scripts/layout.toml. It is the only failure across 61 checks and is unrelated to this slice; the docs edits above leave it the only one.
No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.
No IDE oracle is connected in this run, so the covering-code claims above rest on direct reads of the vet and owner packages -- the weaker basis.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Cache exposure verified absent: the two new finders in VetRepository.java carry no @Cacheable; grep over src/main confirms @Cacheable("vets") appears only on the two pre-existing unfiltered reads (lines 45, 55), whose keys carry no caller-supplied string. CacheConfiguration.java creates only the 'vets' cache and adds no new path that could key on the caller's specialty, so the ADR's decision holds in the code.

XSS on the reflected specialty: every pagination link in vetList.html now uses the parameterized @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})} form; the unencoded __${...}__ preprocessing form is gone from the file. Thymeleaf URL-encodes link parameter values and HTML-escapes th:href output, so a caller value carrying quotes, angle brackets, or & cannot break out of the attribute or inject a further parameter. The null branch omits the parameter entirely rather than emitting an empty one. VetControllerTests asserts both halves (specialty=small%20mammal present, raw 'specialty=small mammal' absent).

Expression injection: the specialty never reaches Thymeleaf's __${...}__ preprocessing or any th:utext sink; it is a model variable consumed as a link parameter, not concatenated into an evaluated expression. The model attribute is used nowhere else in the template.

SQL injection: both finders are Spring Data derived queries (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase), parameterized by the framework, matching the system-design threat-model row that no string-concatenated SQL exists in production code. Multi-valued binding of the parameter collapses to one comma-joined string that matches nothing, with no injection surface.
